The system of linear equations,

$$4x + 2y = 7$$ ...... (i)

$$2x + y = 6$$ ........ (ii)

Multiplying 2 in both sides of equation (ii),

$$4x + 2y = 12$$ ..... (iii)

By comparing equation (i) and (iii), its left hand side is equal. So, right hand side should also be equal. But $$7 \ne 12$$.

Thus, given system is inconsistent and no solution exists.

en.explanation:
Given : $$f(x) = {e^x} + \sin x$$ ....... (i)

The Taylor series expansion for a function f(x) is,

$$f(x) = f(a) + (x - a)f'(a) + {{{{(x - a)}^2}} \over {2!}}f''(a) + ......\infty $$

On comparing, the coefficient of $${(x - \pi )^2}$$ is $${1 \over {2!}}f''(a)$$ [take a = $$\pi$$].

Differentiating equation (i),

$$f'(x) = {e^x} + \cos x$$

$$f''(x) = {e^x} - \sin x$$

Thus, coefficient of $${(x - \pi )^2}$$ at (x = $$\pi$$) is,

$$ = {1 \over {2!}}{\left\{ {{e^x} - \sin x} \right\}_{x = \pi }} = {1 \over 2}{e^\pi } = 0.5{e^\pi }$$
